title: H7 fix round 1: the flaky-rerun subprocess goes through the module's timeout-enforcing runner; the seven acceptance tests at fb696ce stay green (review T-0410)
spec:
STEP 0: the worktree must contain b9c2972 and fb696ce (T-0364, H7 code and its seven acceptance tests) in git log; never drop or amend them. Review T-0410 judged b9c2972 before fb696ce added the tests; its two test findings are answered by fb696ce (confirm the seven tests exist and pass, do not rewrite them). Remaining finding:
1. (med) orchestrator/daemon.py:141 the flaky-rerun call subprocess.run(["pytest", "-q", *ids], cwd=worktree, capture_output=True, text=True) has no timeout, unlike every other subprocess in the module which goes through _run(..., timeout, ...); a hanging test blocks the daemon tick indefinitely. Fix: run the rerun through the module's timeout-enforcing runner (or subprocess.run with a bounded timeout from [daemon].flaky_rerun_timeout_s, default 600, documented in pool.toml); on timeout treat the rerun as not passed (kind stays code_defect or unknown, never flaky) and record the timeout in resume_hint. Also use the worktree's own test runner convention (the same command tests-green.sh uses for this project: unittest when no pytest is available) so the rerun works in projects without pytest. Test: tests/test_daemon.py::test_flaky_rerun_has_timeout_and_timeout_is_not_flaky.
Keep the seven T-0364 tests green. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh from the worktree root until it exits 0, then git add -A and git commit with the task id; report sha and failures only.
acceptance: git log --oneline in the worktree shows fb696ce and b9c2972 below your commit
tests/test_daemon.py::test_flaky_rerun_has_timeout_and_timeout_is_not_flaky passes and grep shows the rerun call carries a timeout
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree
